Content: the order has one recital and one operative sentence. It exempts one named employee, George Cook (plate printer, Bureau of Engraving and Printing, Treasury Department), from compulsory retirement for age under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), for a period of one year ending July 31, 1942. The recital says he "will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service" and asks that he "be exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year". The inventory is therefore one clause, the exemption. Extension reading: this order is the initial exemption; any later exemption of the same person would be a new exercise of the section 204 power with its own period and a later event, not an end of this order, and the packet's searches show none in the held texts.

No held later instrument is shown to keep this exemption operative.

Summerlin from compulsory retirement for age") and EO 9530 of March 14, 1945 ("section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), I hereby exempt the said Harry F. Hawley from compulsory retirement for age"). Their wording shows that section 204 was still the authority for exemptions after this order's last day, so it had not been repealed. No held source shows that any amendment of section 204 extended or extinguished this order's dated exemption, and a later general rule is an end only with a reason it extinguished the command (owner ruling 2026-10-28). The employee's separation, retirement or death would end the practical use of the exemption but is not an instrument ending the command, and none is cited in the packet. Amendments are later events, not ends, and none is found.

Lewis Dalby and ends with the signature "FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT" and the date line "September 22, 1941.". Clauses are quoted from that registered file, not from the unregistered clause-drafts copy.
Content: the order has one recital and one operative sentence. It exempts one named employee, Z. Lewis Dalby (Chief Counsel, United States Employees' Compensation Commission), from compulsory retirement for age under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), for a period of one year ending September 30, 1942. The recital says he "was exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year by Executive Order No. 8538 of September 12, 1940" and asks that he "be further exempted from such compulsory retirement for a period of one year"; the earlier exemption orders it recites are earlier instruments, not later events, and not ends of this order. The inventory is therefore one clause, the exemption. Extension reading: this order is the further exemption; any later exemption of the same person would be a new exercise of the section 204 power with its own period and a later event, not an end of this order, and the packet's searches show none in the held texts.
savings_reason: Service performed and pay earned while the exemption ran are accrued effects of the order; any annuity or retirement-credit consequence flows from the retirement statutes, not from this order, and does not keep the order operative: the order commands nothing after its stated last day (type rule TR-RETIREMENT-EXEMPTION, exceptions_savings: state transferred_or_accrued). No held later instrument is shown to keep this exemption operative.
earlier_end_check: No earlier end found. The only cessation source is the order's own period, "one year ending September 30, 1942". The packet's bounded number search of the held order texts (lookup scope: exactly held_texts(), clause-drafts excluded) found no other held text that cites Executive Order 8905. The Federal Register catalog disposition-note search (later-events:ofr_catalog, checked 2026-10-19) returned no hit for this order. The person-name search of the held order texts (namier:held_texts_person_name, checked 2026-10-28, whose leads list later or undated orders only) found no later order naming Z. Lewis Dalby. Statute check (the type rule research/readiness/type-rules/TR-RETIREMENT-EXEMPTION.json lists a change in the governing retirement statute as a possible earlier end): held APP exemption orders signed after this one still rest on the same section, for example EO 9271 of November 17, 1942 ("section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), I hereby further exempt the said George T. Summerlin from compulsory retirement for age") and EO 9530 of March 14, 1945 ("section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), I hereby exempt the said Harry F. Hawley from compulsory retirement for age"). Their wording shows that section 204 was still the authority for exemptions after this order's last day, so it had not been repealed. No held source shows that any amendment of section 204 extended or extinguished this order's dated exemption, and a later general rule is an end only with a reason it extinguished the command (owner ruling 2026-10-28). The employee's separation, retirement or death would end the practical use of the exemption but is not an instrument ending the command, and none is cited in the packet. Amendments are later events, not ends, and none is found.

The dossier inventory has one whole-order clause (characters 0-667 of the registered file, the recital and the operative sentence); the signature and date line follow it in the full 707-character text. independent_command_check: None found. The order contains one command, the exemption of one named employee; it prescribes no report, procedure, delegation, appropriation or continuing duty. The compulsory-retirement rule it excepts comes from section 204 and the retirement statutes, which are independent of this order, so when the exemption's period ended no command of this order remained to continue.
